newsitem.title: UK: Prompt N.Sea crudes firm as July stragglers sold.
newsitem.headline: Prompt N.Sea crudes firm as July stragglers sold.

text.p: The prompt North Sea crude market adopted a firmer tone on Wednesday as the July stragglers found homes, but concerns about a flood of Iraqi barrels kept pressure on the late summer market, traders said.
A Brent cargo loading July 27-29 was traded between two trading houses at August Brent minus three cents, nine cents up on two deals done on Tuesday.
A million barrels of July-loading Forties also found a home, almost drawing a line under the July market, traders said.
"There may be a couple more passes, but that's basically it," said one.
Early August sales were weaker than the last deals done, with a Forties loading August 4-6 traded at dated Brent +35 cents, and a Flotta loading August 3-5 done at dated Brent -56 cents.
The first August Brents will be nominated loading dates on Thursday.

Western diplomats at the United Nations said on Tuesday that Iraqi exports under the U.N. oil-for-food deal could reach 1.5 million barrels per day in August, or more than twice the average exports flow of the first six months of crude sales.

This is because delays to the start up of the second phase of sales mean that virtually all of the current quarter's $1-billion of exports are set to be concentrated in that month, or Baghdad must forego sales.
"It certainly looks like the market is going to loosen up quite dramatically, but the effect may not hit the North Sea till September...that's why we're seeing Aug/Sept coming in," said one dealer.
The August/September Brent spread firmed steadily over the course of the day, trading at a low of minus five cents and a high of evens.
September/October was steady, trading at -10 cents.
CFDs were better bid by a few cents across the board, although offers were scarce. August 4-8 traded at September Brent -20 cents.
But the outright price was, with bearish sentiment over Iraq countered by a strong U.S. gasoline market buoyed a stock draw of over three million barrels last week.
August Brent was trading four cents lower at $18.35 on the IPE at 1750 GMT.
